_zero_mint_reused._comment: NOT minted — already resolvable, so the sidecar points at these instead. 5 of the 12 slots reuse existing keys because the MERGED WEB PM screens (apps/web/src/screens/pm/wo-detail.tsx) render this same close panel, so the prototype's exact words already live in the dict. Listed so a reviewer can see the mint was minimised rather than skipped; each th was re-read from docs/extract/i18n-full.json this round and asserted byte-exact against the .jsx line by the sidecar test.
_zero_mint_reused.rowAsset: dict pm.fieldAsset — th 'อุปกรณ์' is byte-identical to the prototype's row-1 label (L201)
_zero_mint_reused.rowTotalTime: dict pm.timeTotal — th 'รวมเวลา' byte-identical to the prototype's row-4 label (L201)
_zero_mint_reused.signatureTitle: dict pm.signatureLabel — th 'ลายเซ็นลูกค้า / ผู้ดูแลอาคาร' byte-identical to the signature card title (L205)
_zero_mint_reused.checkProgress: dict pm.checkProgress '{n}/{count} รายการ' — the web PM screen's own count sentence, whose rendered shape is exactly the prototype's '5/5 รายการ' (L201). Fed through tf() with n=checked, count=total. The sidecar test pins that BOTH placeholders survive, so a future edit to the dict entry cannot silently ship a literal '{count}'
_zero_mint_reused.rowParts: phrases 'อะไหล่' — already present in the phrases layer on dev (L201). The parts VALUE is not keyed: pm_workorder has no parts column (parts live on pmQuotes.parts via POST /pm/quotes and carry money), so the kept label renders over an em-dash
_zero_mint_reused.close: dict pm.closeWithSignBtn 'ปิดงาน + ลายเซ็น' — the web close modal's own button key. It replaces the prototype's CTA label (see _not_minted_deliberately.ctaLabel) and sits on a PERMANENTLY DISABLED control (B-288). It names a capability, not an outcome: it does not say a job IS closed

_rejected_near_misses._comment: Existing dict keys that are semantically adjacent but NOT this screen's copy. Recorded so Wei can alias/consolidate instead of minting, if preferred. Each was found by an exact-value scan over all 3701 dict entries + 1065 phrases; none is byte-equal to the prototype string it would replace.
_rejected_near_misses.pm.rowCustomer: 'ลูกค้า / นิติบุคคล' — the web PM contract panel's customer row. Semantically the same slot as the prototype's 'ผู้รับบริการ' caption (L209) but NOT the same words; per the B-061 ruling a near-miss label becomes a new verbatim key rather than a substitution
_rejected_near_misses.pm.timeSummaryTitle: 'สรุปเวลาทำงาน' — the web time panel's title. The prototype's card is 'สรุปงาน' (job summary, L200), which is wider than time alone
_rejected_near_misses.pm.timeStart / pm.timeEnd: 'เริ่มงาน' / 'เสร็จงาน' — two SEPARATE web rows. The prototype fuses them into one 'เริ่ม-เสร็จ' row (L201), so neither key is that label. Both values are em-dashed here anyway (no clock column exists)
_rejected_near_misses.pm.readyToClose: 'ตรวจครบ {count} รายการ · พร้อมปิดงาน' — asserts the checklist is COMPLETE and the job is ready to close. Deliberately unused: it turns an aggregate (checked==total) into a readiness claim, and closing is blocked regardless (B-288)
_rejected_near_misses.pm.closedNote: 'ปิดงานแล้ว · ลูกค้าลงนามรับงาน' — states the job IS closed. There is no status column; see _not_minted_deliberately.successHeading
_rejected_near_misses.pm.signHere: 'ลงนาม ✓' — an imperative on a pad that cannot capture anything (B-288); see _not_minted_deliberately.padHint
_rejected_near_misses.pm.resultRepair: 'เปลี่ยน/ซ่อม (Change-Repair)' — the checklist screen's RESULT-BUTTON label, not the summary's compact 'ซ่อม {n}' tail (L201)

_not_minted_deliberately._comment: Four prototype strings are DROPPED rather than keyed. Each is a CLAIM about state, and a claim cannot be em-dashed the way a missing value can — the pm-notes banner precedent (B-280/B-285). Minting keys for them would leave the screen one edit from making the claim again, so pm_close_sidecar_test.dart asserts that NO sidecar slot RESOLVES to text containing any of them (asserted on the resolved string, not the raw slot, so pointing a slot at an existing dict id such as pm.toastClosed cannot smuggle one back in).
_not_minted_deliberately.successHeading: L189 'ปิดงาน PM สำเร็จ' — announces a completion status. pm_workorder has NO status column and NO certificate column, and the close handler's own comment says close never invents one (apps/api/src/routes/pm.ts L753-760). NB there IS a DERIVED 'done' — apps/web/src/screens/pm/wo-rows.ts deriveStatus L206 reads customerSign != '' — but this screen cannot write customer_sign (B-288), so it can never be the thing that makes a job done, and it must not announce that it was.
_not_minted_deliberately.successSubtitle: L190 'ส่งใบรับรองผล PM ให้ลูกค้าผ่าน LINE แล้ว' — states a PM certificate was pushed to the customer over LINE. No certificate exists anywhere in the schema, and lineNotifyStub is a verified no-op (pm.ts L218-220, B-108b). The whole success view (L185-194) is dropped with it, including its 'กลับรายการงาน' back button (L191), and is unreachable anyway: it is entered by a close this screen cannot perform.
_not_minted_deliberately.ctaLabel: L213 'ปิดงาน PM + ส่งรายงาน' — the 'ส่งรายงาน' half is the same LINE promise as the subtitle. Replaced by the existing dict key pm.closeWithSignBtn on a permanently DISABLED control. This IS a visible deviation from tests/visual/reference/mobile/pm-close.png, and it is not the only one — that image also renders the success-view path, a cursive signature inside the pad, and mock values in the start-end / total-time / parts rows where this port prints em-dashes. B-288 enumerates the set and files it for a ruling.
_not_minted_deliberately.padHint: L207 'แตะเพื่อให้ลูกค้าลงนาม' ('tap to have the customer sign') — promises an interaction the pad does not have. Signature capture is unbuilt (B-288), so the pad renders the STORED customer_sign state and is inert; an instruction to tap it would be a false affordance. The signed state's cursive 'คุณวีรชัย ✓' (L207) and the caption's 'คุณวีรชัย (นิติบุคคล อาคาร A)' (L209) are mock DATA, not keys — the customer name is three hops away and stops at a uuid (contractWire exposes only customer_id, pm.ts L276-288), so the caption's label is kept and its value em-dashed.
